rationale: A wins because it understands the sharpest story is regulatory risk plus the unnamed supply chain: "The FDA Flagged Compounded Semaglutide Risks. Hims Is Prescribing It Publicly." B has solid bones, but it wastes a slot on "Hims & Hers pairs at-home blood testing with prescribing, betting personalization sells better than price," which is product-feature incense before the proof exists. A has hallucination bruises, especially named pharma companies, but it gives a founder the cleaner map of what is pitchable and what needs to be nailed down first.
gaps_in_A: "Novo Nordisk" and "Eli Lilly" are not in the supplied update. The facts say branded manufacturers pushed back; naming the players may be true in the real world, but this exercise asked for update-grounded angles, not memory flexing.
"the clearest test case yet" and "entering the space at scale" overclaim the facts. The update says Hims is launching access; it does not prove scale, uniqueness, or enforcement-test status.
"Hims & Hers Just Hit Profitability. Its First Big Move" invents sequencing and strategic priority. The update says recently profitable, not that this is the first major move after profitability.
"Ozempic's Price Locked Them Out" imports a brand-specific patient story before the update gives an actual price comparison, named patient, or specific branded comparator.
gaps_in_B: "betting personalization sells better than price" is an invented strategy claim. The update says Hims added at-home blood testing to personalize treatment; it does not say personalization is the commercial bet or that it beats price.
"doubles down" is both blacklisted slop and weakly grounded. Nothing in the update establishes a prior GLP-1 commitment that would make this a double-down.
"draws pushback from branded drugmakers" implies this specific launch has already drawn a response. The update only says branded manufacturers have pushed back against compounded versions generally.

"A newly profitable Hims & Hers doubles down..." and "Freshly profitable Hims & Hers bets its next act..." are too close. Both are the same public-company-profitability-plus-FDA-risk story in different jackets.
